policy.pricing_text: FRAs at the 3 Jun close (1x4 3.89, 3x6 3.98, 6x9 4.28, 9x12 4.47 vs WIBOR 3M 3.87) price roughly 60bp of NBP hikes within 12 months. The MPC held at 3.75% on 2 Jun (May CPI eased mainly on food; decisions stay data-dependent); Glapiński (3 Jun): lower May CPI cuts the hike odds, rates are high enough and there is no reason to change or even discuss them. Goldman, Noble and Erste read the 3 Jun conference as dovish; PAP survey (1 Jun): a hold until Q3 2027. May flash CPI 3.1% (29 May; 3.7% expected, -0.3% m/m on food); core 3.0% in April. The fuel VAT and excise cuts run to 15 June (extended 28 May).
policy.risk_text: The MPC turned dovish (Glapiński, 3 Jun: no reason to change or even discuss rates), so FRAs trade oil and the Iran talks; risks: renewed Gulf fighting and the fuel package ending (excise from 15 Jun) lifting CPI; long end: the 17 and 24 Jun sales and the deficit.

macro.projection_text: NBP March projection (4 Mar; data to 19 Feb, war excluded): CPI 50% bands 1.6-2.9% (2026), 1.1-3.7% (2027); central path 2.3% / 2.4% / 2.3% (2026-28), GDP 3.9% in 2026; IMF (14 Apr): 2026 CPI 3.3%; EC (21 May): GDP 3.5% in 2026; OECD (June outlook): CPI 3.7% in 2026, no cuts before Q2 2027. The July projection is the next marker.
macro.fiscal_text: 2025 general-government deficit 7.3% of GDP (GUS EDP, 22 Apr), debt 59.7%; 2026 deficit cap PLN 271.7bn; budget deficit after April PLN 89.3bn (30.1% of the limit); the government's assumptions put the 2026 deficit at ~6.8% of GDP; EC (21 May): 6.5%, debt 64.5%; EKF consensus (2 Jun): 6.9%; windfall-tax bill (75% of margins above the 2025 level +20%) in preparation; fuel package (VAT 8%, price caps, minimum excise) to 15 June (28 May).
macro.fiscal_risk_text: 2026 needs ~56% (MoF, 29 May) financed; budget accounts >PLN 200bn expected at end-May (Drop, 29 May); 3 Jun switch (MoF database): PLN 11.63bn sold (demand 12.84bn) vs 10.90bn bought back (PS0527 7.42bn), net +0.73bn; OK0129 4.812%, PS0731 5.269%, DS0436 5.703%; BGK priced EUR 2bn of FPC bonds (2 Jun). S&P affirmed A-/stable (8 May) and its analyst calls the missing medium-term consolidation the key rating risk (26 May); Scope A negative (15 May); Fitch A- and Moody's A2 have negative outlooks.
macro.backdrop_text: The NBP held at 3.75% on 2 Jun; May CPI 3.1% y/y; Q1 GDP 3.5% y/y (second estimate). Ratings: Fitch A- negative, Moody's A2 negative, S&P A- stable. 3-4 Jun: Glapinski: lower May CPI cuts hike odds; rates are high enough, no reason to change or discuss them; a hike debate would come only with durably higher oil and the end of fuel support. GS, Noble and Erste read it as dovish; yields fell from the morning. MoF switch (3 Jun, MoF database): PLN 11.63bn sold vs 10.90bn bought back (PS0527 7.42bn). OECD: CPI 3.7% in 2026, no cuts before Q2 2027. EC: leeway for energy spending. 4 Jun holiday. Abroad: new US-Iran clashes (US strikes on Qeshm, an Iranian strike on Kuwait airport) while Trump said Iran agreed to forgo nuclear weapons; Brent ~$98, then ~$95. ADP 122k, ISM services 54.5 (prices 71.3) and Logan lifted odds of a 2026 Fed hike to ~85%; UST10 4.50%, Bund 10Y 3.04%; June ECB hike near-certain, 2-3 in 2026; Czech May CPI 2.1%; the US plans new tariffs of >=10% on 60 countries.

calendar.plan_text: MoF June plan (29 May): one switch on 3 Jun (settles 8 Jun; buys back DS0726, PS1026, WZ1126, OK0127, PS0527) and sale auctions on 17 and 24 Jun (PLN 6-12bn each) in OK0129, NZ0331, PS0731, DS0436 and NZ0936; no T-bills; ~56% of 2026 needs financed. 3 Jun switch (MoF database): PLN 11.63bn sold (demand 12.84bn) vs 10.90bn bought back (PS0527 7.42bn), net +0.73bn; OK0129 4.812%, PS0731 5.269%, DS0436 5.703%. BGK priced EUR 2bn of FPC bonds on 2 Jun; FPC switch on 18 Jun (buys back FPC0427).
calendar.timing_text: The Aug 2025-Feb 2026 pattern (auction-day close the cheapest point of the week) comes from a rally regime; March's sell-off broke it and April's auction days cheapened on average. Remaining June operations: 17 Jun, 24 Jun. Next MPC in July, with the NBP projection: a hold is expected.

facts.core_text: Regime: talks stalled and Gulf clashes resumed - Brent back at ~$95-98; the NBP held at 3.75% on 2 Jun while FRAs price roughly 60bp of NBP hikes; the ECB is priced for a June hike, the Fed is priced for a 2026 hike, the BoE is priced for hikes, the CNB is on hold and the MNB is on hold. Poland's 5Y CDS was 51bp and the 10Y spread to Bunds 275bp on benchmark bonds (Erste, 3 Jun close). Strong US data: 85% for a 2026 Fed hike (3-4 Jun).
